newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end the day up 2.69 percent.
newsitem.headline: German shares end the day up 2.69 percent.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended electronic dealings on Tuesday 2.69 percent ahead, after a strong afternoon performance on Wall Street gains and a more stable dollar lifted the market.

Market conditions were favourable for additional gains, traders said, after the Bundesbank left its weekly securities repurchase agreement, or repo, fixed at three percent and signaled for now that German rates would not be raised.
Fears of a rate rise eased further with the announcement of lower-than-expected money supply figures for July.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, ended up 109.90 points at 4,190.45 points. Earlier the 30-share DAX index ended up 91.02 points at 4,169.62 points.
"The fact that the Bundesbank left the repo unchanged means there is no sign of a rate move," said one Frankfurt broker.
"Volumes are pretty thin at the moment, but I reckon that when they do come in to the market, they will be on the buy side," the broker said.

Bayer AG ended up 2.31 marks at 72.60 marks after the chemicals and pharmaceuticals group said net profit for the first half of 1997 rose 13 percent to 1.7 billion marks along with an 11 percent rise in sales to 27.4 billion marks.
Volkswagen AG ended higher after reporting strong first-half results on Monday, up 93 marks at 1,376 marks.
The Wolfsburg-based carmaker on Monday said group net profit rose 73 percent in the first six months of the year.

VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech also said in a television interview on Monday that VW expected a good 700,000 orders in Europe for its new Golf model, to be unveiled on Tuesday in Bonn, in the first year of production.
German banks shares were notably higher after also incurring heavy losses in the previous days.
Commerzbank AG, considered a prime takeover target in growing speculation about further industry mergers, ended up 5.19 marks at 69.20.
Deutsche Bank AG also gained, rising three marks to 114.35 marks, while Dresdner Bank AG ended up 3.06 marks at 80.91.
